result.summary: Implements BIP 95 to add Testnet 5 support to Bitcoin Core and the kernel library. Testnet 5 drops the 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception present in previous testnets, raises minimum difficulty, and activates BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) rules from block 1. Only the top five commits belong to this PR, with the remainder inherited from base PR #35793.
result.problem: Earlier testnets suffer from block storms and difficulty manipulation caused by the 20-minute minimum-difficulty rule, and there is no public test network enforcing the proposed BIP 54 consensus cleanup rules from genesis.
evidence: PR description notes consensus cleanup rules are enforced from the start: 'Relative to Testnet 4 it removes the 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception, raises the minimum difficulty, and enforces BIP 54 from block 1.'

Author references IRC meeting discussion outlining the roadmap: 'since BIP 95 activates BIP 54 from block 1, this depends on #35793 and won't make the v32 feature freeze... Once reviewers are happy with the state of the draft here we can add the Genesis block and the network can get started without being included in a release.'
result.scope_notes: The branch is stacked on PR #35793; only the final five commits belong to this PR. The Genesis block has not yet been mined, and DNS or fixed seed nodes have not yet been configured.
result.changed_since_previous: The branch was rebased onto an updated base branch containing upstream changes and further commits from #35793, but the five commits implementing Testnet 5 are functionally unchanged.
result.card: Adds Testnet 5 (BIP 95), which removes the 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception of earlier testnets, raises minimum difficulty, and enforces BIP 54 consensus cleanup rules from block 1. This addresses testnet difficulty manipulation and provides a live proving ground for BIP 54. The PR is stacked on prerequisite PR #35793 (BIP 54), with only the top five commits specific to this work. It remains in draft awaiting the merge of #35793, genesis block generation, and seed node setup.

risk.why: Bugs in testnet chain parameters or consensus rule activation could cause unintended chain splits or invalid block acceptance on Testnet 5.
